subject: Audit scope: temporal watermarking and rollforward clarity
messages:
From: KPMG Audit Team <security-audit@kpmg.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 scope question: point-in-time vs. rollforward inclusion

Hi Tessa,

Quick question while we prepare the evidence list for Acme's SOC 2 Type II review: for Redwood's production logs and snapshots, can you confirm the intended interpretation of the audit cutover "end moment"? Acme has asked whether the audit period end (2026-07-31) should be treated as:

1) Inclusive to the last UTC second (i.e., up to and including 2026-07-31T23:59:59Z), or
2) Inclusive to the last local-server-day (i.e., server local time midnight cutover), or
3) As an interval endpoint where events that originate in-flight and land after midnight are treated as part of the following period unless explicitly rolled forward via documented migration procedures.

Also — the client wants to know whether Redwood's standard point-in-time evidence (DB snapshots, log manifests, KV-cache checkpoints) captures database state with UTC timestamps, or whether there is any local-time normalization we should be aware of.

If you can confirm which interpretation Redwood follows and list the typical evidence artifacts you provide for a bridge letter / point-in-time confirmation (e.g., backup manifest, stable DB snapshot identifier, JVM/host timezone), that would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Alex (on behalf of the KPMG Audit Team)
[Attachment: audit-request-checklist.xlsx]
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: KPMG Audit Team <security-audit@kpmg.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope question: point-in-time vs. rollforward inclusion

Alex — thanks for the note. Short answers up-front: Redwood timestamps events in UTC by default, and our standard practice is to treat the audit-period end as inclusive to the last UTC second (option 1) unless the customer requests a documented rollforward. We do make exceptions for planned migrations where a documented rollforward procedure is executed.

Two clarifying items so we can package exactly what KPMG and Acme need:
- Do you need a formal "bridge letter" that explicitly states Redwood's UTC-based interpretation for Acme's report, or is a manifest + signed cover note sufficient?
- For rollforwards: do you want the operational runbook + the snapshot ID(s) used in the rollforward included as evidence, or just the high-level confirmation that a controlled rollforward occurred?

I'll pull the manifest and the snapshot identifiers and share the draft bridge letter. Priyom / Marissa — I'm looping you in to confirm the DB snapshot IDs and the host timezone configuration used for Acme during the period.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
From: KPMG Audit Team <security-audit@kpmg.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Samantha Yeo <samantha.yeo@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope question: point-in-time vs. rollforward inclusion

Thanks Tessa — that helps. For audit completeness Acme's external auditor (us) typically wants:

- A short bridge letter signed by Redwood asserting the UTC-inclusive convention for the period ending 2026-07-31 (one paragraph is fine, but must be signed and dated).
- A log manifest listing log file names and final offsets for 2026-07-31 (UTC timestamps preferred).
- DB snapshot manifest with snapshot identifier(s) and the exact timestamp (e.g., snapshot: snap-20260731-UTC-230000).
- If a rollforward is used to include events that settled after UTC 2026-07-31T23:59:59Z, then we need the runbook/operational steps and the snapshot IDs that correspond to pre- and post-rollforward states.

Regarding the bridge letter: a signed PDF with company letterhead is required for our file. The manifest/snapshot files can be plain text or CSV. Please avoid local-time-only timestamps — include both UTC and the server-local timezone if you keep local times in any internal artifact.

We'll accept the artifacts via the shared Drive link or as attachments. If you can get a draft bridge letter and the manifests by EOD tomorrow (Thu 2026-08-06), that will keep the timetable intact for the evidence package.

Regards,
Alex (KPMG)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: KPMG Audit Team <security-audit@kpmg.com>, Samantha Yeo <samantha.yeo@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 scope question: temporal watermarking and rollforward clarity

Alex / Samantha — confirmed and attached: we are using UTC as Redwood's canonical timestamp and treat 2026-07-31 as inclusive to 2026-07-31T23:59:59Z by default. If the customer requests a rollforward we will produce the runbook and pre/post snapshot IDs.

Attached evidence (stubs attached here):
- redwood_log_manifest_20260731.csv (CSV with filenames + UTC end offsets)
- db-snapshot-manifest-20260731.txt (snapshot IDs and UTC timestamps)
- bridge-letter-draft-20260805.pdf (draft, signed by Compliance once final language approved)

Notes: 
- The platform records event timestamps in UTC; we also retain server-local timezone in metadata for diagnostics. Where both appear, artifacts include both UTC and local-zone columns.
- For Acme specifically, there was no rollforward executed during the July 31 cutover window; the snapshots listed in the manifest correspond to the point-in-time state captured at 2026-07-31T23:00:00Z and a stable DB snapshot at 2026-07-31T23:59:59Z.

Next steps: Priyom, please confirm the exact snapshot IDs in the manifest before we finalize the signed bridge letter. Marissa, can you upload the final PDFs to the shared Drive link and mark HBSP-47219?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood_log_manifest_20260731.csv, db-snapshot-manifest-20260731.txt, bridge-letter-draft-20260805.pdf]
